reason: I'll attach the load tray so I can test how the tile handles a load.
expectation: The tray should fit beneath the lift setup, ready for balance testing.

alternatives.reason: The sling and crane may help lift the module later, but the tray seems useful for the initial test.

effect: The load tray is fitted, so I can test an uneven load.
reaction: A straightforward setup step; nothing notable yet.
reason: The off-centre block should reveal whether the tray needs balancing.
expectation: I expect the loaded tray to tilt or otherwise show an imbalance, though the result may differ.

alternatives.reason: The sling and crane may be useful later, but I want to test the load first.

effect: The uneven load makes the tray dip, so it needs balancing.
reaction: The visible tilt makes the balance problem clear.
reason: The sliding counterweight should offset the heavy end.
expectation: I expect to adjust the counterweight until the tray sits level.

alternatives.reason: The crane and sling may be useful later, but they do not address the tilt.

effect: The counterweight levels the tray, but its added weight means the setup needs more lift.
reaction: The trade-off between balance and added load is useful to see.
reason: The current controller may let me adjust the lift for the heavier tray.
expectation: I expect to be able to increase the lift and control it more precisely, though I don't yet know how reliably it will stop.

alternatives.reason: The crane and sling may be useful later, but they don't address the current lift adjustment.

effect: The module now has an adjustable controller; the stop still needs attention.
reaction: A straightforward fitting, with no test result yet.
reason: The power-cut switch addresses the goal of a reliable stop.
expectation: I expect the switch to disconnect power and stop the lift, though it may need testing.

alternatives.reason: The crane and sling may help move the module later, but the stop comes first.

effect: The stop overrides the controller, and the module is powered down and reset before moving.
reaction: The override test makes the stop's purpose clear.
reason: The sling and crane are the only available combination, and they should help move the module.
expectation: I expect the sling to attach to the crane so it can lift the module safely.

effect: The crane now has a sling in place of its basket, ready to move the stopped module.
reaction: Reusing the earlier crane is a satisfying connection.
reason: This is the only available combination and should move the module.
expectation: I expect the crane to lift the powered-down module using the sling.

effect: The crane freed the complete module from the stand, with the test blocks removed and the counterweight reset for the empty tray. The goal is complete.
reaction: Reusing the crane to finish the module felt like a satisfying payoff.

mostWorthwhile.text: Balancing the tilted tray was most worthwhile: it showed both how a counterweight corrects a lopsided load and why its added weight matters.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the controller was a necessary but relatively uneventful step; its result did not yet show a test.

surprise.text: The counterweight levelled the tray but also increased the load, so the module needed more lift.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though preparing the crane was initially only a hint of how it would be used.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how the balanced module helps realise Jo's flying fair, especially after the crane's reuse connected earlier work to this chapter.
